units.title: Paper 1: Socialisation, identity and methods of research

topics.title: 1.1 The process of learning and socialisation

outcomes.text: Explain culture, roles, norms, values, beliefs, customs, ideology, power and status as building blocks of the social construction of reality.
Explain why socialisation shapes behaviour and weigh up the nature versus nurture debate.
Describe how family, education, peer group, media and religion socialise people and exert social control.
Explain the role of structure and agency in the individual-society relationship and contrast structuralist and interactionist views.
Explain why people conform: sanctions, social pressure, self-interest and social exchange.
Describe how order is kept through power, ideology, force and consensus.
Explain deviance and non-conformity through subcultures, under-socialisation, marginalisation, cultural deprivation and social resistance.
Explain how social class, gender, ethnicity and age help construct social identity.
Explain how these identities are changing through globalisation, choice and new or hybrid identities.

topics.title: 2.1 Types of data, methods and research design

outcomes.text: Distinguish primary from secondary data and quantitative from qualitative data.
Assess strengths and limitations of secondary sources: official statistics, personal documents, digital content and media.
Assess strengths and limitations of questionnaires, structured interviews, experiments and content analysis.
Assess strengths and limitations of overt and covert participant and non-participant observation and of unstructured, semi-structured and group interviews.
Outline stages of research design: strategy, questions and hypotheses, sampling frames and techniques, pilot studies, operationalisation, conducting research and interpreting results.
Describe case studies, social surveys, ethnography and longitudinal studies.
Explain mixed methods, triangulation and methodological pluralism.
Explain the positivist approach: scientific method, objectivity, reliability and value-freedom.
Explain the interpretivist approach: verstehen, meaning, subjectivity and validity.
Debate whether sociology can or should follow the natural sciences and the role of values in research.
Explain theoretical, practical and ethical considerations affecting choice of topic and method and the conduct of research.
Explain how research findings can be biased by the sociologist's values and by funding and design choices.
Use validity, reliability, objectivity, representativeness and ethics to judge research methods.

topics.title: 3.1 Perspectives on the role of the family

outcomes.text: Explain functionalist accounts of how the family benefits members and society, and how its functions have changed, including the loss of functions debate.
Explain Marxist accounts of the family serving capitalism: ideological control, reproducing labour and consumption.
Outline feminist responses to functionalist and Marxist accounts of the family.
Explain causes and consequences of changing patterns of marriage, cohabitation, divorce and separation.
Describe nuclear, extended, lone-parent, reconstituted and single-person households, plus other forms where locally appropriate.
Describe organisational, cultural and class dimensions of family diversity.
Debate how diverse families really are and whether the nuclear family still dominates.
Explain New Right and postmodernist views on family diversity.
Explain how the state and social policy influence the family.

topics.title: 4.1 Gender equality and experiences of family life

outcomes.text: Compare liberal, radical and Marxist feminist views on equality and power in the family.
Discuss conjugal roles and gender equality in housework, childcare, power and emotion work.
Debate whether family life is positive or negative for its members.
Explain the social construction of childhood and changes in children's role and position in the family.
Explain how social class, gender and ethnicity affect children's experiences.
Describe the role of grandparents, cross-cultural comparisons and effects of changing life expectancy.
Explain changes in the concepts of motherhood and fatherhood.

topics.title: 5.1 Theories about the role of education

outcomes.text: Explain functionalist views on education creating value consensus and social solidarity.
Explain education and role allocation.
Explain Marxist views of education maintaining the capitalist economic system.
Explain education as ideological control and cultural reproduction.

subtopics.title: New Right and social democratic views

outcomes.text: Compare New Right and social democratic views on education and the economy.
Explain equal opportunity and meritocracy.
Judge how meritocratic education systems are today.
Explain education's importance for life chances and the consequences of underachievement for individuals and society.
Weigh evidence and arguments linking education and social mobility.
Explain the social construction of knowledge.
Explain how power, status, culture, economic demands and gender shape curriculum content.
Explain education and cultural reproduction through the ethnocentric, gendered and hidden curriculum.
Link the curriculum to cultural capital.
Explain the difficulties of defining intelligence.
Assess how far IQ tests are shaped by social factors.
Assess intelligence as an influence on educational attainment.
Explain the relationship between material factors and attainment.
Explain cultural explanations: parental attitudes, values, speech codes and cultural capital.
Explain labelling, ability grouping and pupil subcultures.
Evaluate compensatory education programmes.
Explain racism in schools.
Explain cultural explanations for ethnic patterns in attainment.
Explain links between ethnicity and subcultures.
Explain how ethnicity interacts with social class and gender.
Explain how gender socialisation relates to attainment.
Explain how wider social change, changing female expectations and the crisis of masculinity affect gendered achievement.
Explain gender and subcultures.
Explain how teacher expectations and gendered behaviour shape classroom outcomes.
Define globalisation, glocalisation and global culture and explain the problems of defining globalisation.
Describe cultural, political and economic dimensions of globalisation.
Compare Marxist, feminist, postmodernist, globalist, sceptic and transformationalist views on who benefits.
Explain how globalisation affects identity: ethnic revitalisation, cultural defence and hybrid identity.
Contrast cultural divergence with convergence and homogenisation.
Explain the role of Western ideology in shaping identity and the idea of Westernisation.
Explain the spread of liberal democracy and human rights.
Describe global social movements and attempts to oppose globalisation.
Debate the nation state's role in tackling global social and environmental problems.
Debate globalisation's impact on life chances in developing countries in education, income and health.
Assess how successful transnational organisations are at tackling global inequalities.
Explain global inequality through capitalism, colonialism, post-colonialism and patriarchy.
Explain causes of global migration: immigration, emigration, net migration, push and pull factors, labour patterns and tourism.
Explain positive and negative consequences of migration, including cultural diversity, economic benefits, scarce resource worries and negative perceptions.
Debate who benefits from migration.
Explain why global crimes such as human trafficking, corporate crime and environmental crime have emerged.
Explain who benefits from global crime, including Marxist and feminist views.
Discuss the benefits and challenges of globalisation and new technology for policing and prosecuting global crime.

topics.title: 9.1 Traditional media and the new media

outcomes.text: Describe trends in media organisation: cross-media ownership, digitalisation, conglomerates and social media.
Debate who controls the media.
Distinguish traditional from new media.
Debate whether new media has undermined traditional media.

topics.title: 9.2 Theories of the media and influences on media content

outcomes.text: Explain pluralist theories of the media.
Explain Marxist and neo-Marxist theories of the media.
Explain mass manipulation and hegemony as ways of understanding media content.
Explain the postmodernist contribution to understanding the media.
Explain factors shaping the selection and presentation of news.
Explain censorship as an influence on content.
Explain how the media influences politics through agenda setting, opinion polls and news reporting.

topics.title: 9.3 The impact of the new media

outcomes.text: Explain how new media contributes to globalisation.
Explain new media as a challenge to existing power structures.
Debate digital optimism versus digital pessimism.
Explain the impact of new media on social identities and interpersonal relationships.

topics.title: 10.1 Media representations of class, gender, ethnicity, and age groups

outcomes.text: Describe how different groups are represented in the media.
Explain how the media contributes to gender socialisation.
Explain moral panics around class, gender, ethnicity and age groups.
Explain the relationship between the media and popular culture.
Explain direct effects models, including the hypodermic syringe model.
Explain indirect models: uses and gratifications, two-step flow, normative and cultural effects.
Debate strengths and limitations of the different effects models.
Weigh arguments and evidence on how far behaviour is influenced by the media.

topics.title: 10.3 The impact of the media on behaviour

outcomes.text: Weigh arguments and evidence on whether violent media leads to violent behaviour.
Explain the media's impact on crime, including deviance amplification and moral panics.
Describe positive impacts the media may have on behaviour.
Explain effects of media sensationalism and stereotyping.
Describe ways of defining religion.
Explain difficulties of measuring religious belief.
Explain how class, gender, ethnicity and age relate to religiosity.
Compare religion with other belief systems.
Explain functionalist accounts of religion creating social order and solidarity.
Explain Marxist accounts of religion, oppression and capitalism.
Debate strengths and limitations of functionalist and Marxist views of religion.

topics.title: 11.3 Religion as a source of social change

outcomes.text: Explain Weber's theory of religion and the rise of capitalism.
Compare alternative views on religion and the origins of capitalism.
Explain liberation theology as religion driving social change.
Examine religious movements in politics through cases such as the US Evangelical movement or the Ayatollahs in the Iranian revolution.
Explain the secularisation thesis.
Review evidence for a decline in religious belief.
Debate whether rationalisation is causing religious decline.
Debate whether religion has lost its social significance.
Outline feminist perspectives on religion.
Explain patriarchy and gender inequality in religion.
Describe moves to gender equality in religious organisations and evidence that religion can benefit women.
Discuss whether privatised religion is growing.
Explain spiritual shopping and its value for understanding religiosity.
Debate whether resacralisation is a feature of post-modernity.
Explain the significance of new religious movements and New Age ideas.
Explain the growth of fundamentalism: cultural defence, cultural transition, disengagement, marginality and religious revival.
